text:
Original SASRec samples one negative independently per nonpadding target, uniformly from IDs 1…itemnum using rejection sampling. It excludes the user’s entire training-item set, including items beyond the current prefix; padding ID 0 is never sampled. Repeats across positions are allowed; held-out validation/test interactions are not consulted. An empty eligible pool makes the original rejection loop hang. [Original sampler](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py)

The original data loss is sum over valid positions of [−log σ(positive logit) − log(1−σ(negative logit))], divided by the number of nonzero positive targets, plus regularization. Thus positive and negative BCE terms are each averaged over nonpadding positions and then added; averaging all 2N terms would halve the loss. Stable equivalent: mean[softplus(−positive) + softplus(negative)]. [Original model](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py)

Recommended extension, rather than original behavior: sample K=min(32, eligible count) distinct negatives uniformly without replacement per position, preserving training-history exclusion. Track actual counts and validity masks. For BCE, compute unreduced losses on finite logits, select valid negative losses, and divide each position’s negative sum by max(K,1); average positive-plus-negative terms over valid targets. This preserves BCE-1 scaling when K=1. Never multiply infinite masked BCE losses by zero. For K=0, retain positive-only BCE with zero negative contribution. For restricted-candidate softmax, include the positive and K valid negatives, mask invalid candidate logits to −∞, and use logsumexp(candidates)−positive. K=0 yields exactly zero loss and gradient; retain these zero terms in the valid-target average unless explicitly choosing a different normalization. Remove padding rows before softmax; skip batches with no valid targets.
